title: Gradual privilege reduction and event enrichment playbook
content:
Purpose:

This is a practical playbook for executing an incremental RBAC v2 rollout that reduces existing broad privileges over time ("gradual privilege reduction") while simultaneously enhancing audit events with contextual enrichment to satisfy SIEM evidence requirements. The objective is to minimize user/engineer disruption for product teams (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) while delivering stronger forensics and automation signals for compliance/audit.

Context / problem statement:

- Current entitlement surface contains numerous coarse-grained permissions and a mix of long-lived roles used by services, product infra, and engineers.
- SIEM consumers and compliance reviewers request richer, machine-readable evidence (resource ancestry, request intent, origin of delegation, api route + model id, effective TTL).
- We must avoid a risky global-cutover to RBAC v2. A staged attenuation approach reduces blast radius.

Goals:

1) Produce an operationally safe path to reduce permissions by default while preserving critical workflows.
2) Define a minimal set of audit-event enrichments required by SIEM (and include examples).
3) Provide a migration toolkit and measurable roll-forward/rollback gates.
4) Reduce long-lived overprivileged roles by 60% in first 6 months in a staged manner.

Design principles:

- Principle of least surprise: changes should be toggled and reversible, with clear communication and tooling that surfaces failures early.
- Timebound nudges: introduce TTLs and probation periods to encourage privilege reduction without immediate disruption.
- Evidence-first: every change to entitlement surface must be accompanied by a mapping to an audit enrichment and SIEM field.
- Observability-driven rollout: use Console dashboards to validate errors, false positive rates, and help desk impacts.

Core proposals (high level):

1) Entitlement attenuation patterns
- Soft-deny phase: introduce a "log-only" enforcement mode where RBAC checks are evaluated but not enforced; failures produce high-fidelity evidence events forwarded to SIEM.
- Probation cohorts: assign user/service accounts to cohorts (A: immediate enforcement, B: delayed enforcement, C: extended probation). Cohort assignment rules: business-critical services into A after manual review; tools and SRE in B; developer self-service in C.
- Timebound roles: allow attaching a TTL to elevated grants (e.g., 8h, 7d, 30d). Expired grants automatically degrade to reduced scope.

2) Compact capability model
- Move from many operation-level flags to capability bundles (e.g., model-deploy, inference-admin, telemetry-consume). Capability bundles can be pinned to routes and infra types to simplify mapping and least privilege reasoning.

Audit & evidence enrichment (required fields):

Minimum new fields added to audit events (all fields are structured JSON in log):
- actor.id (existing)
- actor.type (user|service|machine)
- actor.derived_via (direct|delegated|token-exchange|assumed-role)
- resource.type (model|route|project|dedicated-pool)
- resource.id (e.g., model:open-3.1-alpaca)
- entitlement.check (capability-bundle or permission string checked)
- check.result (allow|deny|log-only)
- effective_scope (if allow, what constrained scope — e.g., dataset:read-only; project:1234)
- grant.ttl (ISO-8601 duration or null)
- session.id (to link multi-request flows)
- proto.origin (host-region, ip-subnet, vpc-id)
- proof.reference (link to layered evidence: PR ID, policy-snapshot-id)

Examples: (one-line pseudocode examples)
- Denied inference attempt: {actor.id: u123, actor.type: user, resource.type: model, resource.id: open-3.1, entitlement.check: inference-admin, check.result: deny, session.id: s-53a7, proto.origin: us-west1} 

SIEM export mapping and retention notes:

- SIEM fields should map 1:1 to the enriched audit fields above. SIEM index names: redwood-audit-YYYY.MM.DD.
- Evidence bundles (see proof.reference) must be exported as zipped JSON objects to S3/GCS with content-addressed name and an index pointer in the SIEM event. This keeps the SIEM indices small while preserving full detail for post-mortem.
- Retention: keep summarized audit indices for 1 year; full evidence bundles for 3 years for compliance customers.

Operational rollout plan (phases):

Phase 0: Prep (2–4 weeks)
- Inventory: run permission-usage captures over 30 days across services and users (Console -> entitlement-usage export).
- Define capability bundles and mapping proposal.
- Create cohort assignment heuristics (automated + manual override).
- Add short RFC to teams and schedule brown-bag.

Phase 1: Log-only deployment (4–6 weeks)
- Deploy RBAC v2 policy evaluator with check.result=log-only for all evaluated checks.
- Ship audit enrichment fields to logs and SIEM (indexing partial keys).
- Validate by comparing actual enforcement delta vs. expected usage; run daily signals to identify high-risk denials in log-only.

Phase 2: Probation cohorts (6–10 weeks)
- Move safe cohorts into enforcement (A), keep B/C in log-only.
- Start issuing TTL-based grants for tool accounts; add short-lived tokens for human elevated operations.
- Surface Console charts: denial-rate, helpdesk tickets opened per team, rollback count.

Phase 3: Progressive hardening (ongoing)
- Reclassify cohorts from C->B->A by meeting success gates.
- Introduce automated lease renewal flow for long-running jobs where appropriate.
- Enforce retention/archival policy for evidence bundles.

Rollback & safety gates:

- Fallback toggle: global policy fallback that converts enforcement to log-only within 30s. Implemented as a control-plane flag with auditability.
- Automatic rollback triggers: error-rate spike > 5x baseline for 5m, increased customer-facing 500s for applicable routes, or helpdesk signal threshold.

Migration tooling and helpers:

- entitlement-diff: CLI that compares a role's current grants to proposed capability bundles and computes a minimal attenuation plan.
- temp-grant-operator: microservice to create TTL tokens and emit proof.reference links.
- sim-runner: offline simulator that runs historical request traces through v2 evaluator to estimate denial surface.

Metrics & KPIs to track:

- % of accounts downgraded to capability bundles (target 60% in 6 months).
- Deny/allow ratio in log-only vs enforcement cohorts.
- Mean time to remediate false positives (target < 24h).
- Evidence bundle coverage rate (percentage of events that include a proof.reference).

Open questions / trade-offs:

- How granular should capability bundles be to avoid permission explosion? (trade-off: simplicity vs least-privilege).
- Storage costs for long-term proof bundles vs. SIEM index growth. Proposal: tiered storage with compression and TTL.
- Cross-tenant dual-write semantics for Dedicated and Private customers — need explicit consent and per-tenant toggles.

Communication and change management:

- Publish a "what to expect" short doc for engineers, with examples of self-service grant flows and instructions for creating temporary grants.
- Weekly rollout sync with product and infra owners during Phase 1–2.
- Slack channel: #rbac-v2-rollout for triage, and scheduled office hours for 1:1 remediation.

Action items (owner -> tasks):

- Asha P.: finalize capability bundle list and publish to Confluence (due: 2025-11-12).
- Noah K.: finish sim-runner enhancements and run against last 90 days traces (due: 2025-11-25).
- Lucia R.: implement audit enrichment prototype in staging and open PR for schema changes (GitHub PR #342) (due: 2025-12-02).
- Evan Z.: draft SIEM index retention policy and evidence bundle storage proposal (due: 2025-12-09).

Appendix: quick schema sample (single-line JSON example)

{\n  \"timestamp\": \"2026-02-10T14:22:31Z\",\n  \"actor.id\": \"svc-infer-12\",\n  \"actor.type\": \"service\",\n  \"actor.derived_via\": \"assumed-role\",\n  \"resource.type\": \"model\",\n  \"resource.id\": \"open-3.1-alpha\",\n  \"entitlement.check\": \"inference.invoke\",\n  \"check.result\": \"deny\",\n  \"effective_scope\": \"project:2468\",\n  \"grant.ttl\": \"PT0S\",\n  \"session.id\": \"s-53a7\",\n  \"proto.origin\": \"vpc-cc-01\",\n  \"proof.reference\": \"s3://redwood-evidence/aa12b3c4.json.gz\"\n}

Notes for reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: start with a small set of capability bundles and prove the log-only enforcement pattern. Expect to iterate quickly on the evidence fields based on SIEM consumer feedback.

If you want: I can split this playbook into a shorter exec summary + a runbook checklist for the ops team.
